claims.statement: Five writable sync owners—Vault, Settings, Metrics, Connection History and Device—have separate engines, subscriptions and lifecycle state; History and Device share the deployed zone and record implementation but have kind-filtered journals and distinct consumer scopes.

Vault and Device follow the master iCloud switch; History, Metrics and Settings require their optional selections as well. Unset History defaults on and does not inherit the retired Vault preference or environment.
Desktop starts or pauses five sync owners according to Pro capability; mobile additionally requires an active scene and pauses all five on backgrounding.

CloudSyncLifecycle checks account binding and scoped safety/replica state, commits recovery before zone/network work and engine construction, reconciles eligible journal work and requires all current fetches to succeed before sending; local edits remain journaled while paused or fetching.

Pausing, account retirement and fatal delegate persistence failure invalidate the operation ID, cancel the operation, clear engine identity/scope and send/secret-upload readiness, and schedule engine cancellation in a detached MainActor task; old operations and callbacks cannot reopen uploads, while fatal delegate failure rolls back and reports failure rather than treating expected cancellation as an error.

Account mismatch requires explicit confirmation before a new-account engine is created; confirmation resets the owner's journal before rebinding, drops old tombstones/system fields and requeues live records without preparing or transferring old-scoped quarantine. Environment and ordinary-zone resets requeue the category, whereas destructive purge notifications retire and purge the scoped cache.

Category journals retain versioned envelopes, tombstones, pending intent and CloudKit system fields; deterministic merges requeue local winners, scoped eligibility excludes blocked IDs without clearing intent, and save acknowledgement clears only the matching sent version if unblocked.

Fetched records and serverRecordChanged replies undergo the same validation and quarantine; supported reconciliation saves projection, journal/cloud metadata and unblock together. Physical deletion reconciles against durable replica state and may recreate a surviving local record with cleared system fields, still subject to upload restrictions.
Vault excludes device-local group/package expansion from wire projections, V33 Identity has no lastUsedAt, and Settings leaves debug/review and terminal typography preferences device-local.

Settings syncs credential references rather than secret bytes, marks accepted remote references iCloud-backed and migrates local secrets only with authorization from the current successful fetch under master and Settings selection; fetching, failure and retirement revoke authorization.

AISecretStore verifies an iCloud write before recording the iCloud location and removing the local copy, persists pending deletion before Keychain deletion, and retains the deletion marker to prevent delayed Keychain delivery from reviving a removed secret.

Settings uses distinct SSH, SFTP, workspace and notification preference record types inside its existing zone, allowing older clients to filter unfamiliar types before decoding; validation checks that the decoded kind agrees with its record type.

Safety storage scopes restrictions/recovery by container, environment, account, zone, owner and optional consumer; a new or interrupted scope forces a fresh cursor while retaining journal edits, with recovery committed before automatic engine/network work and held until safe completion.

Outgoing protection filters journal mutations, reconciles restored queue entries and materializes eligible saves/deletes synchronously after current-engine and restriction checks; storage errors fail closed, status separates partial restrictions and upgrade hints from corruption, and at most 250 combined materialized changes enter a batch.

Changed decoder capability IDs force scoped refetch for Vault, Settings and the separate History/Device consumers and checkpoint only after successful fetch/merge; Settings derives its ID from participating V1 kinds, while Metrics currently passes no capability ID. A refetch cannot retrofit unsafe historical binaries or make silently ignored V1 additions safe without a breaking version.

Native ConnectionHistoryItem and DeviceItem use the shared TermindConnectionHistoryV1 zone with separate kind-scoped owners; events may precede Hosts, retain the newest 250 with terminal deletion/overflow tombstones, and clearing events leaves devices. Obsolete Vault-zone History/Device copies are ignored rather than imported or physically cleaned by the current Vault owner.

Both platforms present shared CloudSyncSettingsContent with headerless master toggle and aggregate status/actions followed by Optional Sync in History/Metrics/Settings order, without a separate Vault or Device switch; master enabling is Pro-gated and attempts Host password migration.

V28's local Host model stores SSH connection properties as `port`, `identityID` and `charset`; the V28→V30 lightweight migration retains those property names as SSH fields and supplies default-disabled Telnet settings, while the live Host projection supports separate SSH and Telnet profiles.

Local Host schema migration is independent of cloud format; VaultWireV1 freezes legacy Host SSH keys and defaults, VaultWireV2 adds Host forwarding and SSH Key hardware references, and native History and Device writers remain V1.

The V28 compatibility fixture locally migrates and reopens a store twice through TermindPersistence.makeContainer, verifying SSH settings, default-disabled Telnet, associated Vault/History state and default workspace preferences; it does not test CloudKit replicas.

SyncRecordFormats declares per-kind read/write versions: current Vault Host and SSH Key writers use V2 with V1 readers, other Vault kinds and native History/Device remain V1, and a test-only Host V3 proves independent evolution. Record identity prefixes do not follow format upgrades, and encoding failures throw.

Structured cloud.sync.failed logging includes zone, stage and NSError domain/code without sensitive record/account content or localized descriptions; expected cancellation does not turn a paused or active owner into failure, and the legacy importer is retired.

CloudSyncRecordStateStore durably tracks presence, confirmed deletions and exact in-flight deletion incarnation so a crash or ambiguous delete cannot wrongly acknowledge a newer explicit device recreation; full inventory reconciles missing records before sends.

CloudKit purged and encrypted-data-reset zone notifications retire an owner's engine and purge scoped local cloud cache/metadata rather than recreate the zone; ordinary zone deletion instead resets and requeues the journal.

Vault filters obsolete History/Device IDs out of fetched VaultItem records and outgoing journal mutations without importing their payloads or translating old-zone deletions into local activity; it does not schedule physical cleanup of the obsolete cloud copies. Native History bootstrap uses current local events/devices rather than old Vault clocks and system fields.

Native HistoryCloudRecordV1 uses typed required metadata and event/device live fields, clears optional fields on writes and validates kind/format before interpreting native data; record identity does not change with wire format.

Desktop and mobile composition roots apply accepted remote Settings (including notifications), Metrics, History and Device snapshots to live app models; remote Vault Host route changes or removals trigger workspace, transfer and forwarding cleanup before replacing the Host snapshot and reconciling forwarding configuration.

Mobile constructs its five cloud coordinators only with persistent storage, routes History and Device repository mutations to distinct owners, and reconciles their start/pause on scene activation, preference changes and scene removal under Pro and active-scene gating.

SettingsSyncPersistence atomically commits local settings projections and SettingsSyncJournal mutation intent with rollback on failure; preparing bootstraps existing settings and later-added terminal, SSH, SFTP, workspace and notification preference singletons, and committed edits notify the Settings coordinator.

Settings remote application merges envelopes into the journal and rebuilds the projection from complete journal state rather than replaying accepted remote records through the local edit path; it preserves older provider Vertex settings and local skill packages absent from remote envelopes by recording any resulting local difference, while the coordinator commits system fields and quarantine removal with the merge before notifying app models.
Cloud sync operations launched from start, retry or local-change callbacks run in detached MainActor tasks so they do not inherit CloudKit delegate task-local context when fetching or sending.

Disabled owner selection pauses instead of starting and prevents retry or account-merge confirmation; an account sign-out retires and requires sign-in, while a different account waits for explicit merge confirmation before the new engine is created.

Notification preferences are synced Settings data with independent assistant, terminal and SFTP modes, bell versus system terminal delivery, and a nonnegative duration threshold; an older payload without an SFTP mode decodes to unfocused and system authorization is unnecessary for bell-only delivery.

Settings preparation bootstraps the notification singleton journal envelope for previously bootstrapped stores; local notification edits commit persistence and intent together, and winning remote records or tombstones rebuild the projection without echoing an accepted remote edit.

NotificationPreferencesItem is a distinct type in the existing Settings CloudKit zone and its envelope kind is validated against its record type; the coordinator publishes accepted snapshots to platform app models after transactional application.
PersistentNotificationPreferences enters the lightweight V40-to-V41 SwiftData migration; reopening an upgraded store retains saved notifications and earlier workspace preferences.

NotificationSettingsModel persists validated edits before updating live preferences and applies remote snapshots without saving; active-scene initial authorization is requested at most once across concurrent scenes, only when loaded preferences require system notifications and loading has not failed.

Vault V2 Host decoding requires an explicit agentForwardingEnabled field, whereas V1 Host decoding retains historical defaults; VaultSyncCodec dispatches V1 and V2 by kind and format version instead of silently changing the frozen V1 DTO.

Vault V2 serializes external hardware SSH keys with the frozen wire storage value thisDevice and restores security-key algorithm entries to domain external storage; encoding a software SSH key with external storage throws instead of sending it.

Hardware SSH key entries persist their authenticator reference metadata in the Vault and V45 key row, not Keychain private-key material; the library validates and normalizes these keys to external storage, and connection preparation can resolve destination and jump keys without Keychain access.

Hardware-key availability is determined by its saved reference rather than a Keychain lookup; failed hardware metadata updates/deletes roll back the library, and a V44 store of software keys remains readable after upgrade.

On desktop, Settings navigation is per-window: SettingsPageView routes index, category and detail pages through WindowModel.settingsRoute; parent routes drive back navigation and closing Settings restores the previous content destination, falling back to Vault when its workspace is gone.
The desktop Settings index presents Pro via a paywall rather than a Pro route, exposes Logging directly from the index when debug visibility is enabled, and compiles Developer only for DEBUG builds.

Leaving desktop Settings detail routes discards an unconfigured unnamed provider and a new MCP server without a usable name/namespace, but keeps a skill with written content even if untitled; navigating between provider and model list does not discard the provider.

SettingsKey contains both device-local keys and defaults mirrors of synced preferences: actual Settings journal records come from SettingsSyncSnapshot.recordPayloads, which includes AI configuration, skills, web search, terminal, SSH, SFTP, workspace and notification preferences; a UserDefaults key by itself does not imply CloudKit replication.

Diagnostic reporting consent is a device-local optional UserDefaults choice under the preserved diagnostics.crashReportingConsent key; absent or declined consent does not enable reporting, and DiagnosisController saves a changed choice before notifying the reporter rather than placing it in Settings sync.
